chunks: Call them by the names of their fathers; this is more just in the sight of God. If you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your friends. It will not be a sin upon you for what you made a mistake in, but for what your hearts intentionally did; and God is Forgiving, Merciful.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on naming people when their fathers are unknown?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse (Ayat al-Isnad) is foundational for establishing lineage rights and social identity, with scholars like Al-Tabarsi emphasizing that 'brothers in faith' applies specifically to those of the same religious affiliation. It underscores the principle of 'Isqat' (removal of blame) for unintentional errors in naming, while holding individuals accountable for intentional deviations of the heart, reflecting the Shia focus on both outward compliance and inward sincerity.
